text.p: Italian debt markets ended with a positive undertow despite brief profit taking from a record peak on the front month future towards the end of the session.

The September LIFFE future, buoyed up by continued European convergence hopes, had pushed above the 134.00 barrier to its latest record at 134.13 before succumbing to a bout of profit taking and trading 54 basis points up at 134.00 by 1514 GMT.

On the cash market, the February 2007 Btp ended 33 basis points up at 99.70 with the yield at 6.90 percent and the spread over the benchmark Bund standing at 121 basis points after narrowing to its closest point yet at 117 basis points.
Gains triggered stops above the 133.50 level early before large scale buying set in up to 134.00. "Everyone was buying," a dealer commented, saying foreigners and domestics were all in.
But the rally lost a little steam above 134.00 and started to retrace.
On the EMU front, French central bank governor Jean-Claude Trichet said the government must make further budget cuts.

European Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy was quoted as saying there was no question of the 3.0 percent deficit/GDP ratio criterion being "brutally applied" but the credibility of the euro should, at the same time, not be put at risk.
At home, a senior Treasury official confirmed the government was hoping for a record budget surplus of around 30 trillion lire for June.
